scale.source: Swedish uses the long scale: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000000000: en miljard", "1000000000000: en biljon", "1000000000000000: en biljard"

group_mark.source: CLDR number symbols for Swedish (Babel 2.18.0): decimal ',', group '\xa0'

decimal_mark.source: CLDR number symbols for Swedish (Babel 2.18.0): decimal ',', group '\xa0'

space_groups.source: CLDR number symbols for Swedish (Babel 2.18.0): decimal ',', group '\xa0': digits are grouped by a space

compound_words.source: Swedish writes a number below a million as one word: see the RBNF rules quoted on each entry.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: "miljoner" alone names no number: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "2000000: ←← miljoner[ →→]"

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000000: en miljon", "2000000: ←%spellout-cardinal-reale← miljoner": a count above one takes the plural

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: tjugo[→→]": "tjugoett"

compound_shared_letter.source: Svenska skrivregler: three equal consonants at a compound boundary are written as two (rule quoted from memory, not checked against the page); CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "1000: ettusen[ →→]" is ett + tusen

joiner.source: "en och en halv" (SAOL, "halv"); no joiner stands inside a Swedish number: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: tjugo[→→]"

decimal_marker.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "x.x: ←← komma →→"

minus.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "-x: minus →→"

minus_idioms.source: No Swedish idiom puts "minus" before a positive number.

article_one.source: "en" and "ett" are the indefinite article and the numeral 1: CLDR RBNF sv %spellout-cardinal-reale "1: en", %spellout-numbering "1: ett"
